text:
When NHL.com reported that Nathan MacKinnon would miss 12 weeks with a lower-body injury, the fair question was how Colorado would hold up. So far the answer is: fine, and occasionally absurdly. Last night in St. Paul the Avalanche were down 3-0 late, came back, and won in a shootout on Cale Makar's goal. That is three straight wins, and they have outscored teams 19-8 over their last five. Now Martin Necas is out too, with 29 points in 24 games, and the forward group gets thinner again.

The way they are covering it is visible in the minutes. Brock Nelson has taken MacKinnon's spot and played 24:37 in the first game without Necas. Makar is back from his own absence, and Devon Toews has goals in three straight with nine points in his last 10. Our numbers have Colorado at 97% to make the playoffs even with all of this. The one soft spot is in net, where Scott Wedgewood is projected to start at minus 4.0 goals saved above expected, a long way from the 23.6 he saved last season.

The Sharks come in on a good night's memory. They beat Vegas 4-1 at SAP Center, which per Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest was their first regulation home win over the Golden Knights in the history of the matchup, after Vegas had gone 16-0-3 there. Macklin Celebrini is our likeliest player on either side for two points tonight at 38%, and Ivar Stenberg, this summer's second overall pick, has moved onto his line with Igor Chernyshov out. Michael Misa's name is in trade rumors tied to Detroit's Simon Edvinsson, though the reports disagree on whether he is part of it.

The matchup to watch is special teams: Colorado's power play creates 0.80 expected goals a game, and San Jose's penalty kill gives up 0.97 while the Sharks take 4.4 penalties a night. Both teams played last night.
headline: Avalanche keep winning without MacKinnon
